Name: Rucha Joshi
Bio: Prof Rucha Joshi is an Associate Professor at Plaksha University, specifically in natural biomaterials (silk fibroin, collagen) with transformative engineering education reforms. With a PhD and postdoctoral training in Biomedical Engineering (Purdue University), she holds patents for collagen-based drug delivery and banana-peel biscuits, several publications in engineering education as well as bioengineering, exemplifying her innovative spirit. Her research spans tissue engineering and inclusive pedagogy, where she pioneers metacognition, gamification, and human-centered design, and inclusive education, including women in higher education aspiring to be leaders, and visually impaired students in STEM. She has directed Plaksha's Grand Challenges Scholars Program, served on ASEE's diversity committees, and led NSF-backed initiatives to bridge gaps in engineering education. Recognized with the Chhabria Award (2023) for her professional impact, she's also a Springer-published book author and Maharashtra State literary awardee for her memoir in Marathi. Beyond academia, Prof Joshi is a NAUI-certified diver, Punjab State badminton champion, and advocate for women in STEM, embodying the synergy of science, education, and societal change.

Research_Summary: Prof Joshi's current research develops natural biomaterials and integrated therapy, diagnostics, and sensing platforms for wound care and regenerative medicine. Her group engineers silk fibroin and collagen-based hydrogels, scaffolds, and composites, and studies material–cell and material–microbe interactions. She also researches inclusive engineering education and personalized teaching and learning.
